description: Fix VideoProcessor instantiation and error propagation: Instantiate a real VideoProcessor with YOLODetector, MultiObjectTracker, TrackingStrategy, and AnalyticsEngine in the start_analysis endpoint. Send WebSocket error messages when processing fails (including when video_processor is None). Add detailed console logging with phase, frame, percentage, and FPS during processing.
steps: Modify backend/src/api/routes/analysis.py: Instantiate VideoProcessor with YOLOv8n detector, ByteTrack tracker, appropriate TrackingStrategy based on mode, and AnalyticsEngine. Wrap in try/except to catch model loading failures and return error to frontend.

Modify backend/src/services/background_tasks.py: When video_processor is None, send WebSocket error before returning. Add detailed console logging at each processing stage (loading, detecting, tracking, calibrating, analytics, complete) with frame counts, percentages, and FPS.
Verify frontend AnalysisPage.tsx already handles WebSocket error type messages correctly (it does - no changes needed).
acceptance_criteria: VideoProcessor is properly instantiated with YOLODetector(yolov8n.pt), MultiObjectTracker, appropriate TrackingStrategy, and AnalyticsEngine
If VideoProcessor instantiation fails (e.g., model not loadable, missing dependencies), the error is caught and sent via WebSocket to frontend
When video_processor is None in background_tasks.py, a WebSocket error message is sent before marking the session failed
Console logging shows phase name, current frame/total frames, percentage, and processing FPS
Frontend displays error messages from WebSocket (already implemented, verified working)
findings: All 210 backend tests pass. Frontend build succeeds (TypeScript compilation verified). Frontend test runner (vitest) hangs under bun runtime in this sandbox but the frontend code was not modified (AnalysisPage.tsx already handles WebSocket error messages correctly). The VideoProcessor instantiation uses lazy YOLO model loading so it succeeds even without GPU; actual model loading happens at first frame detection. In test environment, the background task fails with FileNotFoundError since mock MP4 bytes are not real video files OpenCV can open, preserving the existing test behavior (status=failed).
